configuration.note: A line layer is read from a file, taken from the border two study areas share, or drawn on a map. A drawn line needs two positions at least; one click is a place, not a route, and the refusal says so and stays on screen. At most 200 lines are drawn one by one, past which a file is the right instrument. A drawn layer carries source 'drawn' so a reader can tell an observation somebody made from a file somebody published.

ports.note: The two areas are inputs only where the layer is a border, and then both are required: the border is the stretch of the first's outline within the stated distance of the second's. Read from a file, the layer has no inputs.

ontology.note: No ontology mapping yet, and no receipt of its own: the lines are handed on as GeoJSON, and a border's source names the two areas and the distance.

changes.description: A layer of lines already drawn reopened showing the whole world. `fitBounds` ran synchronously at mount, when the dialog's panel still had no size, so it fitted the lines into a viewport of 0 x 0 and chose a zoom for that; the `invalidateSize` added the same day corrected the SIZE afterwards and nothing re-fitted. That first fix settled the tiles and not the view, which is why the basemap came back and the lines stayed a world away. The fit now waits for the first moment the container has width and height, and happens ONCE: re-fitting on every resize would throw away wherever the practitioner had panned the moment the panel changed size or went full screen.

evidence.note:
Unit tested: the order of clicking as the direction, reversing without redrawing, a repeated click as one position, a one-position line refused with how to continue it, names that never collide, the 200-line limit, a drawn layer reopening to be added to, and the end bearing of a line whose last segment has no length (no arrowhead, rather than one at an arbitrary angle). Browser tested on Chromium: a route drawn on the map, refused at one position, finished, named, reversed, applied and run, reaching the Map it is wired to. NOT established: that anything checks a drawn route against the ground it was drawn over, and the arrowhead's bearing is not asserted in a browser test -- it is checked in the static renderer, which computes it the same way.

PANNING (2026-11-24). Browser tested on Chromium: the dialog opens saying dragging pans the map with Start a line unpressed; a click before it is pressed lays down nothing and leaves the table empty; Finish the line before starting one says to start one rather than reporting a line of no positions; Start a line sets its pressed state and the map's crosshair class; and finishing a line clears both. NOT established: that a drag actually pans without laying down a position, which is Leaflet's own click suppression rather than this module's code.

THE FIT (2026-11-24). Browser tested on Chromium: a layer seeded with three drawn lines, reopened, draws them across more than a third of the panel; at the world zoom the same three measured about 2 px of an 1100 px panel, so the assertion has room either side. Measured from what is drawn because Leaflet puts neither zoom nor centre in the DOM.
